content.text: Round 4:

questions.question: Every slice ends in a destination presenting its question and the answer. By slice 5, is that five things or one thing with five pages?

options.label: One app, a page per question (Recommended)
options.description: One marimo app under destinations/, gaining a page each slice. Acceptance is the new page, but you also see the previous answers still standing — a regression in slice 2 shows up while you are accepting slice 3. Matches 'a folder for the destinations' reading as one place, and matches how a stakeholder actually meets a growing product.

options.label: One destination per slice
options.description: destinations/01-.../, destinations/02-.../, each standalone and independently runnable. Slice boundaries are physically obvious and nothing couples one answer to another — the DAR no-cross-dependency rule applied to the consumers too. Costs duplicated scaffolding per slice and gives you no view of the whole.

options.label: One app per persona
options.description: Destinations are grouped by who reads them, so a sales director's questions live together and an operations manager's elsewhere — which is what the blueprint means by a user group. Only earns its keep once two personas genuinely diverge; before that it is one app with an extra directory level.

questions.question: The second source, added in a later slice so one DAB entity is genuinely assembled from two systems. What should it be?

options.label: A synthetic CRM drop with its own ids (Recommended)
options.description: A committed file drop — different cadence, different shape, no API — carrying customers under its own identifiers, overlapping Northwind's by only some rows. Forces the analytical-identifier problem the blog devotes a post to: two systems, two spellings of the same customer, one entity. Also exercises a second dlt pipeline shape without a second network dependency.

options.label: A second public API
options.description: Genuinely another system, genuinely remote, no fabrication involved. The problem is that no public demo API shares keys with Northwind, so integration would have to match on names or countries — which demonstrates fuzzy matching rather than the identity resolution the architecture is actually about.

options.label: A second Northwind endpoint as a separate contract
options.description: Treat Customers or OrderDetails as a second contract feeding the same entities. Zero new infrastructure and it does widen DAB. But both contracts come from one system with one set of identifiers, so it never shows the layer breaking a real source dependency — the thing DAB exists for.

options.label: You name it
options.description: You have a second system in mind — a real extract, a file you can supply, something with its own identifier scheme. Tell me and I will read its shape before the slice that needs it.

questions.question: Naming rules, SQL style, what a measure may be called — where do those live, and what enforces them? The blog argues both sides: encode conventions so nothing needs policing, and keep a document an agent reads.

options.label: One document; tools are the rule where they can be (Recommended)
options.description: A single docs/conventions.md carrying every rule with its reason and severity. Where a tool can check a rule, the tool's config IS the rule and the document only records why; everything else is checked by whoever reviews. No second machine-readable copy, so a clarification takes effect the moment it is written.

options.label: Encoded in the generator, no document
options.description: DAR names are emitted, so they cannot be wrong; DAS names are mechanical from the contract; DAB names are checked by a validator. Nothing to police because nothing can deviate. Clean, but it has no answer for the rules a generator cannot reach — what a measure should be called, when a definition is good enough.

options.label: A document plus a custom linter
options.description: Rules written down and a repository-specific checker enforcing them in CI. Strongest enforcement of house rules a stock tool cannot express. Costs the exact drift the blog warns about: the prose and the regex disagree within a quarter, and the disagreement surfaces as an argument in a pull request.

questions.question: What gates a commit? Every commit has to pass on its own for the red-to-green trail to mean anything.

options.label: Full gate (Recommended)
options.description: ruff for lint and format, a strict type checker over the typed domain model, sqlfluff over every piece of SQL including generated SQL dumped to files, yamllint over contracts and models, pytest for everything — run by pre-commit locally and by CI on every push. Generated SQL held to the same standard as hand-written is what makes the two indistinguishable to a reviewer.

options.label: Lean gate
options.description: ruff and pytest, nothing else. Fast, almost no configuration, and no tool ever blocks a slice for a reason you disagree with. The cost lands on the generated SQL, which is the largest artefact in the repository and the one nobody reads line by line.

options.label: Full gate, SQL advisory
options.description: Everything above, but sqlfluff reports without blocking. Keeps generated SQL under review without letting a linter dialect quarrel stop a slice — DuckDB accepts things sqlfluff does not. Advisory checks are ignored within about three weeks, in my experience.

options.description: One marimo app under destinations/, gaining a page each slice. Acceptance is the new page, but you also see the previous answers still standing — a regression in slice 2 shows up while you are accepting slice 3. Matches 'a folder for the destinations' reading as one place, and matches how a stakeholder actually meets a growing product.
options.label: One app, a page per question (Recommended)

options.description: destinations/01-.../, destinations/02-.../, each standalone and independently runnable. Slice boundaries are physically obvious and nothing couples one answer to another — the DAR no-cross-dependency rule applied to the consumers too. Costs duplicated scaffolding per slice and gives you no view of the whole.
options.label: One destination per slice

options.description: Destinations are grouped by who reads them, so a sales director's questions live together and an operations manager's elsewhere — which is what the blueprint means by a user group. Only earns its keep once two personas genuinely diverge; before that it is one app with an extra directory level.
options.label: One app per persona

questions.question: Every slice ends in a destination presenting its question and the answer. By slice 5, is that five things or one thing with five pages?

options.description: A committed file drop — different cadence, different shape, no API — carrying customers under its own identifiers, overlapping Northwind's by only some rows. Forces the analytical-identifier problem the blog devotes a post to: two systems, two spellings of the same customer, one entity. Also exercises a second dlt pipeline shape without a second network dependency.
options.label: A synthetic CRM drop with its own ids (Recommended)

options.description: Genuinely another system, genuinely remote, no fabrication involved. The problem is that no public demo API shares keys with Northwind, so integration would have to match on names or countries — which demonstrates fuzzy matching rather than the identity resolution the architecture is actually about.
options.label: A second public API

options.description: Treat Customers or OrderDetails as a second contract feeding the same entities. Zero new infrastructure and it does widen DAB. But both contracts come from one system with one set of identifiers, so it never shows the layer breaking a real source dependency — the thing DAB exists for.
options.label: A second Northwind endpoint as a separate contract

options.description: You have a second system in mind — a real extract, a file you can supply, something with its own identifier scheme. Tell me and I will read its shape before the slice that needs it.
options.label: You name it

questions.question: The second source, added in a later slice so one DAB entity is genuinely assembled from two systems. What should it be?

options.description: A single docs/conventions.md carrying every rule with its reason and severity. Where a tool can check a rule, the tool's config IS the rule and the document only records why; everything else is checked by whoever reviews. No second machine-readable copy, so a clarification takes effect the moment it is written.
options.label: One document; tools are the rule where they can be (Recommended)

options.description: DAR names are emitted, so they cannot be wrong; DAS names are mechanical from the contract; DAB names are checked by a validator. Nothing to police because nothing can deviate. Clean, but it has no answer for the rules a generator cannot reach — what a measure should be called, when a definition is good enough.
options.label: Encoded in the generator, no document

options.description: Rules written down and a repository-specific checker enforcing them in CI. Strongest enforcement of house rules a stock tool cannot express. Costs the exact drift the blog warns about: the prose and the regex disagree within a quarter, and the disagreement surfaces as an argument in a pull request.
options.label: A document plus a custom linter

questions.question: Naming rules, SQL style, what a measure may be called — where do those live, and what enforces them? The blog argues both sides: encode conventions so nothing needs policing, and keep a document an agent reads.

options.description: ruff for lint and format, a strict type checker over the typed domain model, sqlfluff over every piece of SQL including generated SQL dumped to files, yamllint over contracts and models, pytest for everything — run by pre-commit locally and by CI on every push. Generated SQL held to the same standard as hand-written is what makes the two indistinguishable to a reviewer.
options.label: Full gate (Recommended)

options.description: ruff and pytest, nothing else. Fast, almost no configuration, and no tool ever blocks a slice for a reason you disagree with. The cost lands on the generated SQL, which is the largest artefact in the repository and the one nobody reads line by line.
options.label: Lean gate

options.description: Everything above, but sqlfluff reports without blocking. Keeps generated SQL under review without letting a linter dialect quarrel stop a slice — DuckDB accepts things sqlfluff does not. Advisory checks are ignored within about three weeks, in my experience.
options.label: Full gate, SQL advisory

questions.question: What gates a commit? Every commit has to pass on its own for the red-to-green trail to mean anything.

answers.Naming rules, SQL style, what a measure: One document; tools are the rule where they can be (Recommended)

content.text: Round 4 — the acceptance loop itself:

questions.question: 'Red and green in a single conventional commit.' What is the red? Something has to fail before the slice's commit makes it pass.

options.label: Two independent answers that must agree (Recommended)
options.description: Each question carries two queries: the expected answer computed straight from das__staged, bypassing DAB and DAR entirely, and the actual computed from dar__uss. Red because dar__uss has no such objects yet; green when the two agree row for row. It tests the thing that actually matters — that routing a number through integration and generation did not change it — and it cannot be satisfied by writing down what the code already does.

options.label: A recorded expected result
options.description: The answer is computed once, reviewed, and committed as a fixture; the test asserts dar__uss reproduces it. Simple, fast, catches any regression exactly. But the first recording is only as right as the query that produced it, and after that the test can only confirm the system still agrees with itself.

options.label: The destination renders
options.description: Red while the page errors or shows nothing; green when it draws the answer. Closest to how you actually accept a slice, and no second query to keep honest. It cannot tell a right number from a wrong one — a chart of incorrect data is just as green.

questions.question: How far does this go before we stop and look at it?

options.label: Six slices, reviewed as they land (Recommended)
options.description: Enough to reach every part of the brief: DAS end to end, DAB with a real entity, generated DAR, a destination, a second entity with a relationship, and the second source that makes integration visible. You accept or redirect each one as it arrives, so stopping early costs nothing and is always available.

options.label: Three slices, then reassess
options.description: The minimum that proves the loop: one question through all four layers, then two widenings. Fastest to a decision about whether any of this is worth continuing, and the least sunk if the shape is wrong. The second source and the multi-entity USS would not be reached, so the parts of the architecture that justify it stay unproven.

options.label: Until the question list runs out
options.description: I draft the prioritised list, we work it top to bottom, and it grows as destinations teach you what to ask next — the blog's loop with no fixed end. Most faithful to the methodology. It also has no natural stopping point, so the decision to stop has to be made deliberately rather than reached.

questions.question: DAB is historized: every attribute keeps its versions. What timestamp dates a version? Northwind has business dates like order_date, but no row-modified column, so no source can tell us when a value actually changed.

options.label: When DAS observed it (Recommended)
options.description: Every entity's effective timestamp is the load timestamp of the DAS row it came from. content.text:
No modified date anywhere in Northwind — eleven entity types, ~70 properties, not one change timestamp. So that resolves to observation time, as you said.

Your TDD point lands, and it invalidates how I framed the red/green question. Let me redo it:

questions.question: You're right that TDD is for functions. So what does 'red and green in a single conventional commit' bind to — which artefacts have to be seen failing first?

options.label: Machinery test-first; data checks land with their build (Recommended)
options.description: Python machinery is genuine TDD: the failing pytest and the code that passes it in one commit. SQL and data checks are not written against a stub — they are assertions about what the built warehouse contains, and they land in the same commit as the pipeline that satisfies them. One commit still contains both a failing-then-passing test and its implementation; nobody pretends a SELECT was designed test-first.

options.label: Everything red first, including the data check
options.description: The question's assertion genuinely is red before the slice — dar__uss has no such objects — so I run it, capture the failure, then build, and land it all as one commit. Uniform discipline, and the failure is real rather than staged. It does mean ordering work around producing a red for SQL, which is the ceremony you just flagged.

options.label: TDD on machinery only; data checks are a separate concern
options.description: Test-first for Python, and the data assertions live outside the red/green rule entirely — they run in CI as gates on the built warehouse, committed whenever they are ready. Cleanest separation of two different kinds of confidence. The slice commit then no longer carries the evidence that the question drove the change.

questions.question: Whatever the commit discipline, something has to establish that the number a destination shows is right. Does the cross-check survive?

options.label: Yes — das__staged vs dar__uss must agree (Recommended)
options.description: Each question carries two queries: one computing the answer straight from staged source, one from the generated USS. CI asserts they agree row for row. It is not a TDD test, it is a reconciliation — and it checks the one thing that could silently go wrong, that passing a number through integration and generation changed it. Costs writing each answer twice.

options.label: Reconcile row counts and totals only
options.description: Assert the coarse things — orders in equals orders out, sum of freight preserved — rather than re-computing every answer two ways. Much less duplication and it still catches dropped rows and fan-out, which are the failures that actually happen. It would not catch a wrong grouping or a mis-joined dimension.

options.label: Eyeball it in the destination
options.description: The presentation is the acceptance, so you look at the numbers and say yes. No duplicated queries, no reconciliation machinery. It puts the entire correctness burden on your attention at review time, every slice, forever.

questions.question: The build has to be driven by something — dlt pipelines, daana-cli install/deploy/execute, the USS generation, the checks. What drives it?

options.label: One CLI: uv run adss ... (Recommended)
options.description: Subcommands per layer — das ingest, das unpack, dab deploy, dab execute, dar build, questions check, and a build that runs the lot. Single entry point for you, for CI, and for the skills to document; and being Python it is the thing the typed domain model is expressed in and the thing the tests test.

options.label: A task runner calling tools directly
options.description: A Makefile or just recipe wiring dlt, daana-cli and small scripts together. Transparent — every step is visible as the command it really is, and there is no abstraction of my own between you and the tools. Harder to test, and the orchestration logic ends up living in shell.

options.label: Scripts per layer, no unified entry
options.description: das/run.py, dab/run.sh, dar/build.py, each standing alone. Maximum layer independence and nothing couples the layers except the data. You lose a single way to build the whole thing, which is what CI and a new reader both want first.

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

  # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
  id: MY_BUSINESS_MODEL           # REQUIRED – unique identifier (letters, digits, underscores)
  name: MyBusinessModel            # REQUIRED – human-readable name
  definition: Core business entities and relationships  # one-liner
  description: |                     # free-text, Markdown allowed

GOTCHAS:
  - dataset_name='das__raw' is SILENTLY renamed to 'das_raw' (dlt collapses the double underscore). Only a WARNING log line tells you. Fix: dlt.destinations.filesystem(bucket_url=..., enable_dataset_name_normalization=False). If DAS/DAB/DAR all use double-underscore schema names, every dlt destination in the project needs this flag.
  - DuckDB read_parquet over a glob defaults to the FIRST file's schema and silently drops columns present only in later files — no error, no warning, just missing data. In an append-only lake where you may add a provenance column, always pass union_by_name => true.
  - max_table_nesting=0 is NOT the answer to 'do not normalise'. It only stops child tables; top-level keys still become snake_cased typed columns. Only the payload+data_type='json' hint (or pre-serialising with json.dumps) gives one column.
  - dlt's `json` data_type is NOT a parquet JSON logical type. parquet_schema() shows BYTE_ARRAY / UTF8 / StringType() — byte-identical to a text column. Anything downstream reading the parquet sees a VARCHAR, so the strict layer must cast, always.
  - _dlt_id is regenerated per load. The same source record has a different _dlt_id in every run (10248 was b6aVmzfAxRVPDA then z8O+0F4oaJbS5A). Never use it as a business or record key — add your own content hash.
  - _dlt_loads, _dlt_pipeline_state and _dlt_version are written as .jsonl even when loader_file_format='parquet'. To get a load's completion timestamp you must read_json_auto() the JSONL, not read_parquet(). Better: put das_extracted_at on every row so das__staged never needs that join.
  - dlt inferred freight as DOUBLE when it normalised the record (approach C). Money silently becomes floating point. The strict layer casting to DECIMAL(18,4) out of the JSON string is the fix — another reason not to let dlt infer.
  - Schema evolution is real and late: ship_region only appeared as a column AFTER the first records that had it null, and it landed at the END of the column list. Column ORDER in the parquet is not stable across loads — never rely on positional access.
  - Filesystem `layout` placeholders are arrow-style tokens ({YYYY}, {MM}, {DD}, {load_id}, {file_id}, {ext}, {table_name}, {schema_name}, {curr_date}) — {year}/{month}/{day} raise InvalidFilesystemLayout. The exception text conveniently lists the full valid set.
  - Relative paths inside a DuckDB view's read_parquet() resolve against the DuckDB process's cwd at QUERY time, not at CREATE VIEW time. A view created from the pipeline directory will break when marimo opens the same warehouse.duckdb from elsewhere. Use absolute paths, or a DuckDB variable/macro for the lake root.
  - Two identical runs produce 240 rows for 120 distinct orders. Append-only is correct for DAS but das__staged as written duplicates rows — a dedup/latest-version step (QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY order_id ORDER BY das_extracted_at DESC)) is needed before DAB consumes it.

OPEN:
  - Deduplication strategy between das__raw and das__staged was NOT designed or tested. Two runs gave 240 rows / 120 distinct orders. Does DAB want the full append history, or a latest-version view? This changes whether das__staged is a plain cast view or a QUALIFY/ROW_NUMBER view.
  - Whether enable_dataset_name_normalization=False also disables TABLE name normalisation was not tested — every table name I used was already snake_case. If a source entity is named 'OrderDetails' it may still normalise to 'order_details'; verify before relying on literal names.
  - Not tested: whether DuckDB views over the parquet glob can live inside the SAME warehouse.duckdb that daana-cli installs into, and whether daana-cli's `install`/`deploy` tolerates extra user-created schemas (das__raw, das__staged) in that file.
  - Not tested at scale: 120 rows only. Memory/throughput behaviour with the full 830 Orders (or a large entity) and the cost of DuckDB scanning hundreds of small per-load parquet files was not measured. Small-file accumulation is the obvious risk of one file per load per table.
  - Not tested: incremental extraction (dlt's `dlt.sources.incremental`) against OData — I paginated manually. Whether a cursor on OrderDate/ModifiedDate coexists cleanly with the opaque single-JSON-column design is unverified.
  - Not tested: reading the parquet lake through DuckDB from a remote/object-store bucket_url (httpfs/s3fs). Only local filesystem was exercised, even though s3fs 2026.7.0 was installed.
  - Not tested: what happens when the OData API returns a non-200 or a malformed page mid-pagination — whether the load package is marked failed and whether partial pages are left in the lake.

  [observed] `_dlt_id` is a per-row-instance surrogate, NOT a stable record identity. The same source record (OrderId 10248) got a different _dlt_id in each load. Content identity must come from your own hash column.

  G: max_table_nesting=0 is NOT the answer to 'do not normalise'. It only stops child tables; top-level keys still become snake_cased typed columns. Only the payload+data_type='json' hint (or pre-serialising with json.dumps) gives one column.

======================================================================
SPIKE 4 — quality gate (ruff, ty, sqlfluff, yamllint, pytest, pre-commit) on ADSS-shaped a :: works-with-caveats
======================================================================
HEADLINE: Every tool works and the whole gate goes green from a local venv with zero network: sqlfluff 4.3.0 has a real `duckdb` dialect that parses QUALIFY and quoted `"order"` cleanly, and `ty --error all` catches frozen-dataclass mutation, Literal-discriminator violations and union arg errors with no false positives — the only real fight is four sqlfluff rules (AL09, RF06, LT05, LT09) that structurally contradict how a code generator emits SQL and must be excluded, not fixed.
VERSIONS: Python 3.12.3, uv-managed project, requires-python >=3.12, ruff 0.16.6, ty 0.0.78, sqlfluff 4.3.0, yamllint 1.38.0, pytest 9.1.1, pre-commit 4.6.2, transitively installed by the above: cfgv 3.5.0, chardet 7.6.0, click 8.4.2, colorama 0.4.6, diff-cover 10.5.1, distlib 0.4.3, filelock 3.32.5, identify 2.6.19, iniconfig 2.3.0, jinja2 3.1.6, markupsafe 3.0.3, nodeenv 1.10.0, packaging 26.3, pathspec 1

CLAIMS:
  [observed] sqlfluff 4.3.0 ships a first-class `duckdb` dialect, inheriting from postgres. No stand-in needed.
  [observed] The duckdb dialect is REQUIRED, not merely nicer: the same file under `postgres` fails to parse the QUALIFY clause entirely.
  [observed] On well-formatted generated SQL (UNION ALL of 3 branches, every column AS-aliased, cast(x AS DECIMAL(28,8)), lower-case functions, UPPER keywords, QUALIFY row_number() OVER (...), quoted reserved word `dab."order"`), the ONLY rule that fires under sqlfluff defaults is RF06. Running with `--rules all` produces an identical result, so the default rule set is already everything.
  [observed] The quoted reserved word `dab."order"` is NOT flagged by RF06 — sqlfluff's duckdb dialect knows the quoting is necessary there. Only mixed-case identifiers are flagged.
  [observed] Realistic single-line generator output (no pretty-printing) fires 7 distinct rules. This is the real fight list.
  [observed] AL09 is the single most dangerous rule for this build. The brief's own requirement — 'each branch aliasing every column of one fixed column list with AS' — is exactly what AL09 forbids. It fired twice on `o.order_id AS order_id` and `o.order_status AS order_status`. It did NOT fire in file 1 only because every column there happened to be wrapped in cast() or lower().
  [observed] `sqlfluff fix` auto-repairs CV11 and LT14 but cannot repair RF02. Autofix rewrote `c.customer_name::VARCHAR` to `cast(c.customer_name AS VARCHAR)` and broke WHERE/GROUP onto their own lines.
  [observed] `ty` 0.0.78 IS viable. At DEFAULT severity it already catches all three deliberate errors in the frozen-dataclass / StrEnum / Literal-discriminated-union module: wrong argument type against a `A | B | C` union alias, assignment to a frozen dataclass field, and an out-of-Literal discriminator value.
  [observed] ty in STRICT mode (`--error all`) produces ZERO false positives on the good domain module — no friction from `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`, `StrEnum`, `tuple[Column, ...]`, `field(default_factory=tuple)`, the `A | B | C` union alias, or `match`/`case`/`assert_never` exhaustiveness.
  [observed] ty has no `strict = true` preset in 0.0.78 — strictness is the CLI flag `--error all` (or `--warn`/`--ignore` per rule, or `[tool.ty.rules]` severities in pyproject.toml). `ty check --help` lists `--error <RULE>` with 'Use "all" to apply to all rules'.
  [observed] ty --error all catches Any-leakage and bare generics that mypy --strict catches (`missing-type-argument`, `unsound-return-statement`), but does NOT flag a fully unannotated `def f(x, y)`. That gap must be closed by ruff's ANN rules, which do flag it.

  - ty is 0.0.78 — pre-1.0, pre-release version numbering. It works and is fast, but pin it exactly in uv.lock and expect diagnostic names/severities to churn. There is no `strict = true`; strictness is `--error all` on the CLI. If ty churn becomes intolerable the fallback is mypy --strict, but nothing observed here argues for it.
  - ty --error all does NOT flag fully unannotated functions. If you rely on ty alone for 'strict', untyped defs slip through. Ruff's ANN ruleset (ANN001/ANN201) is what closes that gap — keep ANN in the ruff select list or the type gate has a hole.
  - pre-commit's `ruff format` hook fails the run when it reformats a file ('files were modified by this hook'). That is expected pre-commit behaviour, but in CI it means the format hook is effectively a `--check`. Either accept the re-run, or use `ruff format --check` in the CI-only config.

# Build ADSS as blog.daana.dev describes it

## Context

`mattiasthalen/adss-2026-09-07` is empty apart from a README. The task is to build an
Analytical Data Storage System exactly as the Daana blog describes one — three layers, one
direction of flow — and to do it in thin vertical slices, each answering one business question
and ending in a destination that presents that question and its answer.

I read the four named posts in full myself and the remaining fourteen with one agent each, then
consolidated them into a constraint map. That surfaced **46 decisions the blog does not settle**.
The interview settled the ones that matter; four throwaway spikes settled the ones only a machine
could answer. This plan is what those two exercises produced.

**Prior art**: `mattiasthalen/ADSS-fable-POC` carries a complete previous run at this brief on
fourteen branches. You told me to ignore it, so nothing from it is carried forward. Where this
plan lands where that one did, it is because the blog and daana-cli left one option.

---

## Decisions taken in the interview

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | Prior art ignored. Everything derived from the blog, the brief, and the spikes. |
| 2 | One DuckDB file. The platform sits behind one seam so a swap is a connections change plus a dialect. |
| 3 | Northwind OData first; a synthetic CRM file drop as a second source in slice 6. |
| 4 | Destination is one marimo app, gaining a page per slice. |
| 5 | Six slices, each reviewed as it lands. |
| 6 | Stacked branches, one PR per slice. |
| 7 | The domain model is the **machinery's** own, typed, in code. No business word under `src/`. |
| 8 | One shared `dar__uss`, with the departure from the DAR no-shared-structures principle registered. |
| 9 | DAS lands the whole payload; contracts generate the typed views that unpack it. |
| 10 | USS event and measure declarations live in a sidecar `dab/uss.yaml`. |
| 11 | Record the source once; replay the recording everywhere. |
| 12 | Each skill is written in the slice that builds what it describes. |
| 13 | One `docs/conventions.md`. Where a tool can check a rule, the tool's config **is** the rule. |
| 14 | Full quality gate: ruff, ty, sqlfluff, yamllint, pytest — pre-commit and CI. |
| 15 | Machinery is test-first. Data checks land in the same commit as the build that satisfies them. |
| 16 | Every question is computed twice — from `das__staged` and from `dar__uss` — and the two must agree. |
| 17 | One CLI: `uv run adss …`. |
| 18 | DAB history is dated by **when DAS observed the row**. |
| 19 | Acceptance is a screenshot in the slice's PR; the app also runs locally. |

On (18): Northwind's `$metadata` has eleven entity types and ~70 properties and **not one
modified/updated/version column**, so observation time is the only history the platform can
honestly claim.

---

## What the spikes established

Four spikes ran in scratch and were deleted. Findings kept at
`scratchpad/spike-findings.json`. These are the ones that change the design:

**dlt — DAS landing**
- `@dlt.resource(columns={"payload": {"data_type": "json"}})` yielding a dict under `payload`

  blank offline. Screenshots come from `marimo export thumbnail --execute` (`--execute` is *not*
  the default and without it the thumbnail is empty).
- Playwright wants a chromium build the image does not have; a symlink shim fixes it without
  `playwright install`.
- The app opens the warehouse `read_only=True` and must be stopped while DAB executes.
- DuckDB `DECIMAL` cannot be encoded by altair — DAR aggregates cast to `DOUBLE`.

**The gate**
- sqlfluff 4.3.0 has a real `duckdb` dialect, and it is required — `postgres` cannot parse
  `QUALIFY`.
- Exclude `AL09` (it forbids the every-column-aliased discipline that makes UNION branches safe),
  `RF06`, `LT05`, `LT09`. Keep `RF02` — it is a correctness rule and the one sqlfluff cannot
  autofix. The generator emits `cast()` exclusively for `CV11`.
- `ty --error all` catches frozen-dataclass mutation and discriminated-union violations with zero
  false positives, but does not flag unannotated defs — ruff's `ANN` closes that hole.
- All pre-commit hooks run from the local venv; no network, so CI determinism is under `uv.lock`.

---

## Repository layout

```
das/contracts/*.yaml      one contract per source entity set; documentation, schema and
das/fixtures/             transformation in one artefact. Recorded payloads.
dab/model.yaml            the only place the data is explained
dab/uss.yaml              events and measures, keyed by entity/attribute id
dab/mappings/*.yaml       one per entity
dab/workflow.yaml         daana workflow
dab/connections.yaml      duckdb profile: target dab, stage dab__stage, metadata dab__meta
dar/sql/                  generated USS SQL, committed and drift-checked
destinations/app.py       one marimo app, a page per question
questions/NN-<slug>.md    the business questions: story, W's, definitions, both queries
src/adss/                 the machinery and its typed domain model
tests/
docs/blueprint.md         principles, technology-free
docs/conventions.md       the one convention document
docs/deviations.md        the register (D-0001: one shared dar__uss)
docs/adr/                 MADR, numbered, superseded rather than edited
.claude/skills/{adss,das,dab,dar,destination}/SKILL.md
```

Schemas in the one warehouse: `das__raw`, `das__staged`, `dab`, `dab__stage`, `dab__meta`,
`dar__uss`.

CLI: `adss das record|ingest|unpack`, `adss dab install|deploy|execute`, `adss dar build`,
`adss questions check`, `adss destination shoot`, `adss build`.

---

## The six slices

Each widens the system by exactly one architectural thing. **Draft — cut and reorder before
slice 1 starts.**

| # | Persona | Question | What it widens |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sales director | How many orders were placed per order month and ship country? | The whole spine, once: one contract, one entity, one transaction event, one count measure, bridge + peripheral + calendar, one page |
| 2 | Logistics manager | What freight did we pay per customer country and order quarter? | Second contract, second entity, first relationship, **key inheritance** (customer country is not ship country), first sum measure |
| 3 | Operations manager | How many orders shipped per shipping month, and how many days did they take? | Two events on one entity, second bridge stage, "an unshipped order has no shipment event", ratio computed at query time from two additive measures |
| 4 | Finance analyst | What revenue did we take per order month? | A third entity at a **finer grain** (order lines), a derived measure, and the fan-trap proof: freight must not multiply across lines |
| 5 | Category manager | What revenue did we take per product category and quarter? | Two more contracts and a **two-hop relationship chain** (line → product → category) |
| 6 | Sales director | What revenue did we take per customer segment and quarter? | **The second source.** A CRM file drop with its own customer identifiers, overlapping Northwind's on only some rows; segment exists nowhere else. One entity assembled from two systems |

Slice 6 is where the architecture earns its keep: it is the only slice whose question is
unanswerable without the integration layer.

---

## How a slice runs

MADR before the code, in every slice. One workflow per slice, plus workflows wherever else they
help.

1. **Frame** — a workflow fans out two agents: one drafts the options and consequences for the
   single decision this slice forces, quoting the blog; one audits what already binds it
   (blueprint, conventions, deviations, prior ADRs) and reports any rule the slice would break.
2. **Decide** — I write the MADR from that, and commit it. `docs(adr): …`
3. **Build** — main loop. Machinery is test-first: the failing pytest and the code that passes it
   in one conventional commit. The question's two queries and the data checks land in the commit
   that makes them true.
4. **Verify** — a workflow fans out four independent lenses: a layering audit (does anything read
   across a boundary?), a convention audit, an **independent recomputation** of the answer from
   the recorded fixtures using none of my code, and a test-quality audit (would these tests fail
   if the implementation were broken?). I act on what survives.
5. **Present** — `adss destination shoot` produces the thumbnail; PR opened with the screenshot,
   the question, and both queries.

Branches stack: `claude/adss-blog-implementation-vy62ci` is the trunk and carries the scaffold;
`claude/adss-slice-01-…` branches off it, `…-02-…` off that, each PR targeting the one below.
**This is a departure from the single-branch instruction I was given, and it is what you chose —
approving this plan authorises those branch pushes.**

Spikes, when a slice hits something neither of us can answer: time-boxed, run in scratch, findings
recorded in the ADR that consumed them, code deleted. Never landed.

---

## Verification

- `uv run adss build --offline` rebuilds the whole warehouse from recorded fixtures, no network.
- `uv run adss questions check` recomputes every question both ways and fails on any disagreement
  — the check that says routing a number through integration and generation did not change it.
- `uv run pytest` — machinery tests, plus a fan-out test proving a parent measure is not
  multiplied by its children, plus a test that `DESCRIBE dar__uss._bridge` matches the plan.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` — the full gate, offline.
- `uv run marimo run destinations/app.py` — the app you accept on.
- CI runs all of the above on every push; a scheduled job hits the live Northwind API and fails
  loudly if the recording no longer matches.

## Deliverables

The six slices; the typed machinery domain model; five skills (`das`, `dab`, `dar`,
`destination`, `adss`), each written in the slice that earns it; the blueprint, conventions and
deviations register; one MADR per decision.

## First commit

Scaffold on the trunk: `pyproject.toml` (Python 3.12, uv), the gate configs the spike proved
(`.sqlfluff` with the duckdb dialect and four exclusions, `.yamllint.yaml`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`,
ruff/ty/pytest config), CI, `docs/blueprint.md`, `docs/conventions.md`, `docs/deviations.md` with
D-0001, `docs/adr/0000-use-madr.md`, and the `adss` CLI skeleton with `--version` under test.

content.text:
Two things. Taking the second first:

**No — Verify as I wrote it is neither.** The four lenses are ADSS-specific (layer boundaries, conventions, an independent recomputation of the answer, test quality). Generic code review and security review are separate, and this session has `/code-review` and `/security-review` skills for exactly that. I left them out; that was an omission, not a decision.

On hive partitioning: agreed, and the spike found dlt's `layout` takes literal text around its placeholders, so `orders/das_extracted_year={YYYY}/...` produces true `key=value` directories that DuckDB reads with `hive_partitioning => true`. It leaves the partition key open, which is a question:

questions.question: What partitions the landing zone? dlt writes one parquet file per table per load, so the layout string decides the directory keys DuckDB then prunes on.

options.label: Extraction date: year / month / day (Recommended)
options.description: das__raw/<table>/das_extracted_year=2026/das_extracted_month=09/das_extracted_day=07/<load>.parquet. Prunes on the axis DAS actually owns — when the platform observed the data — which is the same clock that dates every DAB version. Three levels is shallow enough not to shatter small tables into thousands of files.

options.label: Extraction date plus load id
options.description: The same three levels with a load_id= directory beneath, so a single load is addressable as a path and can be replayed or excluded without touching a file list. Load id is already unique in the filename, so this mostly buys a tidier predicate at the cost of a fourth level and unbounded directory cardinality.

options.label: Load id only
options.description: One directory per load, nothing else. Exact, trivially explainable, and re-reading one load is a single path. No date pruning at all, so any question about a window has to scan every load — which is the thing partitioning exists to avoid.

options.label: Extraction month only
options.description: Two levels, year and month. Far fewer directories on a source that reloads often, and still prunes any question with a time window. Day-level replay becomes a file-list operation rather than a path.

questions.question: Given that, what should the per-slice Verify fan-out actually run?

options.label: The four lenses plus /code-review (Recommended)
options.description: Layering, conventions, independent recomputation, test quality — plus a real correctness review of the slice's diff. Security gets one pass at the end over the whole system rather than six times over a local analytics prototype whose only surfaces are generated SQL, a connections file and a localhost bind.

options.label: Both reviews, every slice
options.description: Add /security-review to the above on every slice. Nothing accumulates unexamined, and the SQL-generation and credential-handling surfaces get looked at while they are being built rather than after. Costs a review pass per slice on a system with no auth, no untrusted input and no network service.

options.label: The four lenses only
options.description: Keep Verify strictly about whether this architecture did its job, and run code and security review yourself when you want them. Leanest, and it keeps the fan-out focused on what no generic reviewer would catch. Ordinary bugs in the machinery would then only be caught by the tests I wrote for it.

**Partitioning and the provenance clock**

`_dlt_load_id` is a unix-epoch string, and it is the single provenance fact the whole platform's
time axis derives from — in two shapes, never two clocks:

- **Landing** is hive-partitioned one level deep:
  `das__raw/<table>/extracted_on=YYYY-MM-DD/<load_id>.<file_id>.parquet`.
- **`das__raw` views** read it with `hive_partitioning => true`, `union_by_name => true`, and
  `hive_types` so `extracted_on` comes back `DATE` rather than `VARCHAR`. Any question with a
  time window prunes on it.
- **`unpack` casts a copy of `_dlt_load_id` into `das__staged.<table>.extracted_at`**
  (`to_timestamp(cast(_dlt_load_id AS DOUBLE))`), and *that* column is what
  `entity_effective_timestamp_expression` points at — so DAB's history clock and the landing
  zone's partition key are the same fact, derived twice.
- `unpack` asserts `extracted_on = cast(extracted_at AS DATE)`, which catches the one way they
  can diverge: a load that starts before midnight and writes after it.

Two things to confirm in slice 1, both cheap and both under test: that `{YYYY}-{MM}-{DD}` renders
inside one path segment, and whether those placeholders take the load's clock or the writer's.

# Build ADSS as blog.daana.dev describes it

## Context

`mattiasthalen/adss-2026-09-07` is empty apart from a README. The task is to build an
Analytical Data Storage System exactly as the Daana blog describes one — three layers, one
direction of flow — and to do it in thin vertical slices, each answering one business question
and ending in a destination that presents that question and its answer.

I read the four named posts in full myself and the remaining fourteen with one agent each, then
consolidated them into a constraint map. That surfaced **46 decisions the blog does not settle**.
The interview settled the ones that matter; four throwaway spikes settled the ones only a machine
could answer. This plan is what those two exercises produced.

**Prior art**: `mattiasthalen/ADSS-fable-POC` carries a complete previous run at this brief on
fourteen branches. You told me to ignore it, so nothing from it is carried forward. Where this
plan lands where that one did, it is because the blog and daana-cli left one option.

---

## Decisions taken in the interview

| # | Decision |
|---|---|
| 1 | Prior art ignored. Everything derived from the blog, the brief, and the spikes. |
| 2 | One DuckDB file. The platform sits behind one seam so a swap is a connections change plus a dialect. |
| 3 | Northwind OData first; a synthetic CRM file drop as a second source in slice 6. |
| 4 | Destination is one marimo app, gaining a page per slice. |
| 5 | Six slices, each reviewed as it lands. |
| 6 | Stacked branches, one PR per slice. |
| 7 | The domain model is the **machinery's** own, typed, in code. No business word under `src/`. |
| 8 | One shared `dar__uss`, with the departure from the DAR no-shared-structures principle registered. |
| 9 | DAS lands the whole payload, hive-partitioned; contracts generate the typed views that unpack it. |
| 10 | USS event and measure declarations live in a sidecar `dab/uss.yaml`. |
| 11 | Record the source once; replay the recording everywhere. |
| 12 | Each skill is written in the slice that builds what it describes. |
| 13 | One `docs/conventions.md`. Where a tool can check a rule, the tool's config **is** the rule. |
| 14 | Full quality gate: ruff, ty, sqlfluff, yamllint, pytest — pre-commit and CI. |
| 15 | Machinery is test-first. Data checks land in the same commit as the build that satisfies them. |

**Prior art**: `mattiasthalen/ADSS-fable-POC` carries a complete previous run at this brief on

| 1 | Prior art ignored. Everything derived from the blog, the brief, and the spikes. |
| 2 | One DuckDB file. The platform sits behind one seam so a swap is a connections change plus a dialect. |
| 3 | Northwind OData first; a synthetic CRM file drop as a second source in slice 6. |
| 4 | Destination is one marimo app, gaining a page per slice. |
| 5 | Six slices, each reviewed as it lands. |
| 6 | Stacked branches, one PR per slice. |
| 7 | The domain model is the **machinery's** own, typed, in code. No business word under `src/`. |
| 8 | One shared `dar__uss`, with the departure from the DAR no-shared-structures principle registered. |
| 9 | DAS lands the whole payload, hive-partitioned; contracts generate the typed views that unpack it. |
| 10 | USS event and measure declarations live in a sidecar `dab/uss.yaml`. |
| 11 | Record the source once; replay the recording everywhere. |
| 12 | Each skill is written in the slice that builds what it describes. |
| 13 | One `docs/conventions.md`. Where a tool can check a rule, the tool's config **is** the rule. |
| 14 | Full quality gate: ruff, ty, sqlfluff, yamllint, pytest — pre-commit and CI. |
| 15 | Machinery is test-first. Data checks land in the same commit as the build that satisfies them. |
| 16 | Every question is computed twice — from `das__staged` and from `dar__uss` — and the two must agree. |
| 17 | One CLI: `uv run adss …`. |
| 18 | DAB history is dated by **when DAS observed the row**. |
| 19 | Acceptance is a screenshot in the slice's PR; the app also runs locally. |

modified/updated/version column**, so observation time is the only history the platform can
honestly claim.

Four spikes ran in scratch and were deleted. Findings kept at

  lands the whole record in one column with **no** inference and **no** child tables.

  `enable_dataset_name_normalization=False`.

  files. Every view needs `union_by_name => true`.

  record identity. DAS must add its own provenance columns.

  two-layer design recovers precision the one-layer design loses.

  which raises).

`_dlt_load_id` is a unix-epoch string, and it is the single provenance fact the whole platform's
time axis derives from — in two shapes, never two clocks:

- **Landing** is hive-partitioned one level deep:
  `das__raw/<table>/extracted_on=YYYY-MM-DD/<load_id>.<file_id>.parquet`.

  `hive_types` so `extracted_on` comes back `DATE` rather than `VARCHAR`. Any question with a
  time window prunes on it.

  (`to_timestamp(cast(_dlt_load_id AS DOUBLE))`), and *that* column is what
  `entity_effective_timestamp_expression` points at — so DAB's history clock and the landing
  zone's partition key are the same fact, derived twice.
- `unpack` asserts `extracted_on = cast(extracted_at AS DATE)`, which catches the one way they
  can diverge: a load that starts before midnight and writes after it.

  `daana-cli execute`**, and the error it reports is a lie ("framework is not installed").

  built on the `view_*` layer only.
- **`view_<entity>_with_rel` carries no relationship keys** despite its name. Relationship keys
  come from `view_<src>_<rel>_<tgt>`.

  attributes are widened to `DECIMAL(28,8)` regardless of source type.

- All pre-commit hooks run from the local venv; no network, so CI determinism is under `uv.lock`.

das/fixtures/             transformation in one artefact. Recorded payloads.
das/lake/                 hive-partitioned parquet: <table>/extracted_on=YYYY-MM-DD/*.parquet
dab/model.yaml            the only place the data is explained
dab/uss.yaml              events and measures, keyed by entity/attribute id
dab/mappings/*.yaml       one per entity
dab/workflow.yaml         daana workflow
dab/connections.yaml      duckdb profile: target dab, stage dab__stage, metadata dab__meta
dar/sql/                  generated USS SQL, committed and drift-checked
destinations/app.py       one marimo app, a page per question
src/adss/                 the machinery and its typed domain model
tests/
docs/blueprint.md         principles, technology-free
docs/conventions.md       the one convention document
docs/deviations.md        the register (D-0001: one shared dar__uss)
docs/adr/                 MADR, numbered, superseded rather than edited
docs/questions/NN-<slug>.md   the business questions: story, W's, definitions, both queries
.claude/skills/{adss,das,dab,dar,destination}/SKILL.md
```

The top level is the four folders the brief names — `das/`, `dab/`, `dar/`, `destinations/` —
plus `src/`, `tests/`, `docs/` and `.claude/`. Questions are documentation, so they live under
`docs/` with the rest of the writing.

Schemas in the one warehouse: `das__raw`, `das__staged`, `dab`, `dab__stage`, `dab__meta`,
`dar__uss`.

CLI: `adss das record|ingest|unpack`, `adss dab install|deploy|execute`, `adss dar build`,
`adss questions check`, `adss destination shoot`, `adss build`.

---

## The six slices

Each widens the system by exactly one architectural thing. **Draft — cut and reorder before
slice 1 starts.**

| # | Persona | Question | What it widens |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sales director | How many orders were placed per order month and ship country? | The whole spine, once: one contract, one entity, one transaction event, one count measure, bridge + peripheral + calendar, one page |
| 2 | Logistics manager | What freight did we pay per customer country and order quarter? | Second contract, second entity, first relationship, **key inheritance** (customer country is not ship country), first sum measure |
| 3 | Operations manager | How many orders shipped per shipping month, and how many days did they take? | Two events on one entity, second bridge stage, "an unshipped order has no shipment event", ratio computed at query time from two additive measures |
| 4 | Finance analyst | What revenue did we take per order month? | A third entity at a **finer grain** (order lines), a derived measure, and the fan-trap proof: freight must not multiply across lines |
| 5 | Category manager | What revenue did we take per product category and quarter? | Two more contracts and a **two-hop relationship chain** (line → product → category) |
| 6 | Sales director | What revenue did we take per customer segment and quarter? | **The second source.** A CRM file drop with its own customer identifiers, overlapping Northwind's on only some rows; segment exists nowhere else. One entity assembled from two systems |

Slice 6 is where the architecture earns its keep: it is the only slice whose question is
unanswerable without the integration layer.

---

## How a slice runs

MADR before the code, in every slice. One workflow per slice, plus workflows wherever else they
help.

1. **Frame** — a workflow fans out two agents: one drafts the options and consequences for the
   single decision this slice forces, quoting the blog; one audits what already binds it
   (blueprint, conventions, deviations, prior ADRs) and reports any rule the slice would break.
2. **Decide** — I write the MADR from that, and commit it. `docs(adr): …`
3. **Build** — main loop. Machinery is test-first: the failing pytest and the code that passes it
   in one conventional commit. The question's two queries and the data checks land in the commit
   that makes them true.
4. **Verify** — a workflow fans out four ADSS-specific lenses: a layering audit (does anything
   read across a boundary?), a convention audit, an **independent recomputation** of the answer
   from the recorded fixtures using none of my code, and a test-quality audit (would these tests
   fail if the implementation were broken?) — **plus `/code-review` over the slice's diff** for
   ordinary correctness, which none of those four would catch. I act on what survives.
   `/security-review` runs once at the end over the whole system rather than six times: the only
   surfaces here are generated SQL, a connections file and a localhost bind.
5. **Present** — `adss destination shoot` produces the thumbnail; PR opened with the screenshot,
   the question, and both queries.

Branches stack: `claude/adss-blog-implementation-vy62ci` is the trunk and carries the scaffold;
`claude/adss-slice-01-…` branches off it, `…-02-…` off that, each PR targeting the one below.
**This is a departure from the single-branch instruction I was given, and it is what you chose —
approving this plan authorises those branch pushes.**

Spikes, when a slice hits something neither of us can answer: time-boxed, run in scratch, findings
recorded in the ADR that consumed them, code deleted. Never landed.

---

## Verification

- `uv run adss build --offline` rebuilds the whole warehouse from recorded fixtures, no network.
- `uv run adss questions check` recomputes every question both ways and fails on any disagreement
  — the check that says routing a number through integration and generation did not change it.
- `uv run pytest` — machinery tests, plus a fan-out test proving a parent measure is not
  multiplied by its children, plus a test that `DESCRIBE dar__uss._bridge` matches the plan.
- `uv run pre-commit run --all-files` — the full gate, offline.
- `uv run marimo run destinations/app.py` — the app you accept on.
- A partition-pruning test: a windowed question reads fewer parquet files than the lake holds,
  and `extracted_on` equals `cast(extracted_at AS DATE)` on every landed row.
- CI runs all of the above on every push; a scheduled job hits the live Northwind API and fails
  loudly if the recording no longer matches.

## Deliverables

The six slices; the typed machinery domain model; five skills (`das`, `dab`, `dar`,
`destination`, `adss`), each written in the slice that earns it; the blueprint, conventions and
deviations register; one MADR per decision.

## First commit

Scaffold on the trunk: `pyproject.toml` (Python 3.12, uv), the gate configs the spike proved
(`.sqlfluff` with the duckdb dialect and four exclusions, `.yamllint.yaml`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`,
ruff/ty/pytest config), CI, `docs/blueprint.md`, `docs/conventions.md`, `docs/deviations.md` with
D-0001, `docs/adr/0000-use-madr.md`, and the `adss` CLI skeleton with `--version` under test.

entries.name: TaskCreate
entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

subject.description: A brief title for the task

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

metadata.description: Arbitrary metadata to attach to the task

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

taskId.description: The ID of the task to update

activeForm.description: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")

addBlocks.description: Task IDs that this task blocks

addBlockedBy.description: Task IDs that block this task

metadata.description: Metadata keys to merge into the task. Set a key to null to delete it.

cat > pyproject.toml <<'EOF'
[project]
name = "adss"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "An Analytical Data Storage System: DAS, DAB, DAR, and the destinations that read them"
readme = "README.md"
authors = [{ name = "Mattias Thalen" }]
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "altair>=6.2.2",
    "dlt[filesystem,parquet]>=1.30.0",
    "duckdb>=1.5.5",
    "marimo>=0.24.0",
    "polars>=1.44.1",
    "pyarrow>=25.0.1",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
    "typer>=0.27.2",
]

[project.scripts]
adss = "adss.cli:app"

[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build>=0.8.17,<0.9.0"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "playwright>=1.62.0",
    "pre-commit>=4.6.2",
    "pytest>=9.1.1",
    "ruff>=0.16.6",
    "sqlfluff>=4.3.0",
    "ty>=0.0.78",
    "yamllint>=1.38.0",
]

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ruff is the Python style. See docs/conventions.md section 5 for the reason.
# ANN is not optional: ty does not flag a fully unannotated def, and ANN does.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "SIM", "ANN", "RUF"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/*" = ["ANN201"]

[tool.ty.environment]
python-version = "3.12"
root = ["./src", "./tests"]

[tool.ty.rules]
possibly-unresolved-reference = "error"
unused-ignore-comment = "error"

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
addopts = "-q --strict-markers"
EOF
cat > .sqlfluff <<'EOF'
# The SQL style. docs/conventions.md section 3 records why each setting is what it is.
# The duckdb dialect is required, not preferred: postgres cannot parse QUALIFY.
[sqlfluff]
dialect = duckdb
templater = raw
max_line_length = 120
# AL09 forbids `x AS x`, which is exactly the every-column-aliased discipline that makes a
# UNION branch positionally safe. RF06 fires on every mixed-case identifier crossing over from
# DAB. LT05 and LT09 are line-layout opinions a generator should not have to implement.
exclude_rules = AL09, RF06, LT05, LT09

[sqlfluff:indentation]
indented_joins = false
indented_using_on = true

[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.keywords]
capitalisation_policy = upper

[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.functions]
extended_capitalisation_policy = lower

[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.identifiers]
extended_capitalisation_policy = consistent

[sqlfluff:rules:capitalisation.types]
extended_capitalisation_policy = upper

[sqlfluff:rules:convention.casting_style]
preferred_type_casting_style = cast
EOF
cat > .yamllint.yaml <<'EOF'
# docs/conventions.md section 4. yamllint walks into .venv by default and floods on
# third-party YAML, so the ignore is mandatory rather than cosmetic.
extends: default
ignore: |
  .venv/
  .git/
rules:
  document-start: disable
  line-length:
    max: 160
    allow-non-breakable-words: true
    allow-non-breakable-inline-mappings: true
  truthy:
    check-keys: false
  braces:
    min-spaces-inside: 0
    max-spaces-inside: 1
EOF

# Every hook runs from the local uv venv. Nothing is fetched, so what CI runs is pinned by

default_install_hook_types: [pre-commit]
fail_fast: false
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: ruff-check
        name: ruff check
        entry: uv run --frozen ruff check --force-exclude
        language: system
        types_or: [python, pyi]
        require_serial: true
      - id: ruff-format

        entry: uv run --frozen ruff format --force-exclude
        language: system
        types_or: [python, pyi]

      - id: ty

      - id: sqlfluff-lint
